evidence: deepseek: "# Johnson's rule"; gpt-oss: "# Johnson's rule"; glm-5: "group1 ... sort by p1 ascending" and "group2 ... sort by p2 descending"
affordance_in_statement: The mainframe is responsible for computing the specifications for the orders. It can only process one order at a time. You must choose the sequence in which the mainframe processes the batch. Once started, the mainframe will work continuously through your chosen sequence without any idle time. Once the mainframe finishes an order, that order immediately becomes available for the testing rig. The testing rig also processes one order at a time. It always selects the available order that finished its mainframe computation earliest.
secondary_shortcut_name: explicit FIFO availability and continuous first-machine processing
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove the two-machine flow-shop structure; it is the core task. To hide the canonical shortcut, re-present the process as an abstract event-driven completion system with neutral resource names and define the resulting completion times indirectly, without explicitly describing a continuously running first machine feeding an earliest-finished FIFO second machine.
